faq: Which languages and frameworks do you work in?
Mostly JavaScript and TypeScript with React, Next.js and Node.js, plus Python, PHP and Laravel. If your stack is different, send the repository link and we tell you before you order.
Do you need access to my live system?
No. We work in your repository and a test environment. You or your team deploy the finished change, or we do it if you give us deployment access.
What if the codebase is messy?
We work with it as it is and keep our change small and clear. If something in the way needs repairing, we tell you what and why before changing it.
Can you add a feature without a written spec?
Yes, a short description plus screenshots or examples is enough. We confirm the details back in writing before we start, so we both agree what done looks like.
desc:
Adding features to an existing codebase means extending a live website or app without breaking what already works. Ecom Swift LLC reads your repository, builds the new feature or fix on a separate branch and sends a pull request for your review before anything goes live.

## What is feature work on an existing codebase?

Feature work is the development of a new capability, a bug fix or a tidy-up inside code that already exists. The developer does not start fresh. They study the current structure, follow its conventions and change only what the task needs. The result arrives as a pull request: a reviewable set of changes that you or your team approve before merging.

## Why changing existing code needs care

New code placed in an old project can quietly break something far away. A change to a shared function affects every screen that uses it. A database change run without a plan can lose records. A fix that ignores the project's style makes the next developer's job harder.

Careful feature work respects what is already there. It starts by reading, keeps the diff small, adds tests where they protect the change, and never touches the live product without approval. That discipline is what separates a clean addition from a patch that causes three new bugs.

## How well-made changes affect your product and budget

A finished feature is a visible gain: customers can do something new, and your team stops doing it by hand. A fixed bug removes a source of support emails and lost trust. A tidied module makes every later change faster and cheaper, because the next developer meets clearer code.

Review gives you control. Because the work sits on a branch, you can read each change, ask questions and request edits. If you decide to delay or drop the feature, your live product is untouched.

## What great feature work includes

- A written description of the feature, agreed before coding starts.
- A reading pass over the related code, so the new work matches the existing patterns.
- All changes on a separate branch, never directly on your main branch.
- Code that follows your naming, formatting and folder conventions.
- Tests for the new code where they make sense.
- A database change script when the data structure must change, so the update can be repeated safely.
- A pull request with clear notes on what changed and why.
- Responses to your review comments.
- A short deployment note describing how to release the change.
- A handover explanation for larger changes, covering the parts that were touched.

## What we do

You share the repository and describe what you want. We read the relevant code, confirm our understanding with you and build the change. The Basic package covers one small feature or a few bug fixes with a pull request. Standard handles a medium feature or a batch of fixes, adds tests, includes a database script if needed and covers one round of review changes. Premium takes on a larger feature across the front end and back end, tidies the touched area and finishes with a call to explain the work.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Describe the outcome in plain words, with an example of how a user would see it.
- Share screenshots, error messages and steps to reproduce bugs.
- Name the person who will review the pull request.
- Keep a recent backup before any database change.
- Tell us about parts of the code that are fragile.

**Avoid:**
- Bundling unrelated requests into one task.
- Changing the requirements halfway through the build.
- Merging without reading the pull request.
- Testing only on your live site.
- Asking for a refactor of the whole project inside a small feature.

## Who this is for

This service suits a business owner whose developer left and who needs a new checkout option or report. It suits a small team with a backlog of bugs and no free hands. It also suits a founder whose app has a rough module that every new feature has to work around.

## What we need from you

Send access to the repository as a collaborator, a clear description of the feature or bugs, and instructions for running the project locally. A written spec helps, but a short conversation is enough to start. We do not need access to your live system or any passwords. After you order, we reply with a checklist and keep you updated until the pull request is ready.
